This small plot here at home I keep mostly for our food — it is intercropped the way we always do, and the soil here has been worked for many seasons. I do not buy chemical fertilizer; the price is too high for me, but I carry manure from our few animals and kitchen ash to spread on the plot. I use the seed we keep from last season like my mother taught me, and I weed by hand with my daughter when she comes from school. The rains usually come well enough here in Kagera, so I do not need to water, and I cannot afford to hire many workers for such a small piece.
